analysis.investment_thesis: Aditya Vision scores well on ROCE (~30%) but fails catastrophically on earnings yield — at an EBIT of INR 175 Cr against an EV of ~INR 7,214 Cr, earnings yield is only ~2.4%, far below the 12%+ threshold the Magic Formula demands. The market has priced in years of perfect execution, leaving no margin of safety.
key_strengths: Strong ROCE of ~30% signals genuine business quality — good inventory turns and asset efficiency for a retailer
Impressive 36% revenue CAGR (2022→2025) demonstrates rapid store expansion and demand capture in underserved Bihar/East India market
Promoter holding of 47% with FII + DII interest of 35%+ reflects institutional conviction in the growth story
key_risks: Earnings yield of ~2.4% (EBIT INR 175 Cr / EV INR 7,214 Cr) — Magic Formula rejects anything below 12%
Free cash flow deeply negative and worsening: INR -13 Cr (2023) → -41 Cr (2024) → -78 Cr (2025); operating CF also turned negative
Thin operating margins (~6.6%) typical of consumer electronics retail leave no cushion — any revenue slowdown or pricing pressure destroys profitability
red_flags: Negative OCF for 2 consecutive years (-6 Cr in FY24, -41 Cr in FY25) despite strong reported profits — earnings are not converting to cash
Debt jumped from INR 319 Cr to INR 480 Cr in a single year; financing CF positive only because of external borrowings, not business generation
P/E of 61x and EV/EBITDA of 36x for a 6.6% operating margin retailer — valuation assumes flawless execution for a decade
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running Aditya Vision through the Magic Formula: EBIT = INR 175 Cr, Enterprise Value = Market Cap (6,759.7) + Debt (480) – Cash (26) = INR 7,213.7 Cr. Earnings Yield = 2.43% — this is nearly the worst possible score on the cheapness axis. The formula demands >12%; anything below 6% is a hard pass. On the return-on-capital side, the reported ROCE of ~30% is genuinely impressive, implying capital employed of roughly INR 584 Cr — a testament to good inventory management in a regional electronics retail franchise. But one excellent metric does not make a Magic Formula stock; BOTH must rank highly, and on price this fails completely.

The deeper concern is cash flow. Net profit grew from INR 35 Cr to INR 106 Cr (44% CAGR), yet operating cash flow went from +INR 32 Cr (2022) to –INR 41 Cr (2025) and FCF is –INR 78 Cr last year. This divergence signals aggressive working capital build-up as stores expand — not inherently disqualifying, but it means the business is consuming, not generating, cash. The entire expansion is being funded by debt (up 50% in one year). At P/E 61x and EV/EBITDA 36x, the market is pricing in sustained 30%+ growth with margin expansion. There is zero margin of safety; Greenblatt's approach would rank this near the bottom of any screened universe.
